# Lazy loading

*Concept* · also written lazy-loading · lazy-loaded

Loading images or content only when they come into view; Google sees it only if it works without scrolling or clicks.

**Glossary** (*Lazy loading*): Loading content only when it is needed. Triggered by an Intersection Observer it can work for Google; triggered by scroll events or clicks it does not.

Narrative: the topic [Lazy loading and content behind interactions](../topics/lazy-loading.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

6 claims mention it: 1 from Google's documentation, 3 shown or said at the event (1 confirmed by Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Fix lazy-loaded content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading).

- [`D2-C276`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Docs: To make infinite scroll indexable, Google's lazy-loading guide says to support paginated loading: give each chunk its own persistent, unique URL, link sequentially to those URLs, and update the displayed URL with the History API when a new chunk becomes the main visible element. `[D2-C276, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C198`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Lazy loading should be triggered by an Intersection Observer that watches a sentinel element instead of by a scroll event listener. `[D2-C198, slide, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C197`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Lazy loading triggered by a scroll event listener, such as window.addEventListener('scroll', loadMoreProducts), never runs for Googlebot because Googlebot does not scroll. `[D2-C197, slide, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C199`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: An Intersection Observer fires when the observed element enters the viewport, and the viewport Google renders with is tall, so content lazy-loaded this way can load during rendering. `[D2-C199, slide, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C203`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: Audit tabs, accordions and 'load more' lists for content fetched on click or scroll: put tab content in the initial DOM and hide it with CSS, trigger lazy loading with an Intersection Observer, and give long lists paginated URLs linked with `<a href>`. `[D2-C203, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C275`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Analysis: Treat the 10,000-pixel viewport as a safety margin, not a target: load lazy content when it enters the viewport (Intersection Observer or native lazy loading, never scroll listeners), and give infinite-scroll content paginated URLs linked with `<a href>` so anything below the first rendered screen stays reachable. `[D2-C275, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-REN-03` **MUST** · Documented: Lazy-load with native lazy loading or an IntersectionObserver, never with scroll events (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
